newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds fall on profit-taking after surge.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds fall on profit-taking after surge.

text.p: Argentine bonds fell Wednesday as the market finally caved in to a bout of profit-taking after three days of rallying prices.
Traders said it was natural the market fell back after the sharp rise of recent sessions, particularly since much of the strong run was fuelled by gains by other Latin American markets.
"There was profit-taking, a correction," said a trader at an Argentine bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.20 to 119.40, and Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 3/8 to 84-1/4.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Provisional 2 due 2007 fell $0.55 to 104.35.
The market turned around from early gains, when it rose on the back of talk of a Brazilian bond issue and of a possible upgrade of Brazilian debt by the credit rating agencies.
"A decline was to be expected, not because the strong sentiment has changed, but because it's not possible to sustain a market in a continuous rise," said another trader.
The first trader noted that feeling, saying that trade was much busier in the morning when the market was rising than in the afternoon when it fell.
Separately, the Economy Ministry said Wednesday gross domestic product rose 2.6 percent in the second quarter but fell 0.2 percent in the first half of the year.
In the money markets, call money was unchanged at 6.36 percent.
